However, this usefulness come at the expense of the usability of these devices in some contexts. Thus, usability becomes an important factor in the adoption of mobile applications (such as mobile tracking applications, mobile health and mobile learning), which are often used by people who have problems when using mobile devices and who have a limited experience of technology. Based on three research questions, the results indicated that, there are three kinds of the Mobile tracking applications namely: information tracking, location tracking and information and location tracking. result.paraphrase: In recent years, mobile devices have been considered useful because they let users carry out more tasks in a mobile context. However, this usefulness comes at the cost of usability in some situations. As a result, usability is a key factor in the adoption of mobile applications, such as mobile tracking, mobile health, and mobile learning apps, which are often used by people with limited technology experience or difficulty using mobile devices. Ensuring the success of mobile applications in the mobile domain is critical. Although some studies have reviewed usability evaluation, there are unfortunately no systematic literature reviews focused on the usability evaluation of mobile tracking applications. Therefore, this study aims to present the findings of a systematic literature review (SLR) on the use of usability evaluation techniques in mobile tracking applications. Based on three research questions, the results showed three types of mobile tracking applications: information tracking, location tracking, and combined information and location tracking. Regarding the techniques used to assess usability, experimental studies were the most commonly used in the selected studies. Finally, the results indicated that the characteristics most frequently used to measure the usability of mobile tracking applications are effectiveness, efficiency, usefulness, and accuracy. This study is valuable for researchers who need to evaluate the usability of new mobile applications by identifying appropriate evaluation methods and the indicators required for this purpose.
